evolution_hints.conditional_prediction: Treat S as a model-conditional covariate rather than a compulsory predictor. evolution_hints.decisive_holdout: Use preregistered condition-level splits with at least one wavelength, one substrate or cap-thickness condition, and one independent preparation held out. Require calibration-consistent interval coverage and complexity-adjusted error for both models, and repeat the split after hierarchical covariance re-estimation.

unresolved_attacks.countermodel: Let an unmeasured adsorption-state mixture U vary with cap thickness, morphology, and wavelength. U changes the relative Raman band ratios through mode-specific chemical polarizability and also changes coverage, molecular sampling location, and the optical observables used to construct S. unresolved_attacks.countermodel: Suppose repeated spectra contain condition-dependent covariance not captured by C: laser-history effects, spatially correlated hot-spot sampling, multiplicative detector drift, and shared uncertainty in the orientation and Raman-tensor estimates. unresolved_attacks.independent_discriminator: Acquire independent preparations with randomized wavelength, position, polarization, and dose order; estimate full replicate covariance; use blinded calibration standards and a held-out instrument-response check; compare the S interaction before and after covariance re-estimation.

evolution_hints.conditional_prediction: Let y be the log relative-band-ratio vector, let y_O be the orientation-only prediction, and let C be the combined measurement and model covariance. Define χ²_O=(y−y_O)^T C^{-1}(y−y_O), with effective degrees of freedom reported rather than assigning universal cutoffs. Define S independently from preregistered, mode-relevant variation in excitation/Stokes transfer functions, local polarization, and molecularly weighted spatial sampling; estimate uncertainty in S. Conditional prediction: in low-S conditions, the distribution of χ²_O should be compatible with its calibrated error distribution; in high-S conditions, orientation-only misfit should increase relative to that calibration and the broader known-physics model should improve held-out predictive score. The association may be nonmonotonic with wavelength or cap thickness, so the preregistered test should use an uncertainty-weighted interaction or prespecified smooth function rather than require monotonic growth. Operational labels such as orientation-consistent, ambiguous, and field-selective-inconsistent may be reported only as descriptive classifications, not physical thresholds.

Fit chemical-state terms before electromagnetic transfer terms, then compare nested models on held-out band-ratio vectors, interval coverage, and uncertainty-weighted error without refitting condition-specific scales.

evolution_hints.conditional_prediction: Common scaling of transition rates predicts a shorter temporal correlation time and reduced time-averaged intensity covariance, but no intrinsic kinetic change in band-ratio dispersion when state-emission vectors are proportional. A rate-dependent ratio effect and any stronger heterogeneous-field interaction are conditional on independently verified nonproportional, field-dependent spectral directions. The stationary pooled mean ratio remains invariant under pure common-rate scaling.
evolution_hints.decisive_holdout: Train models only on prespecified training windows and compare held-out predictions for total-intensity covariance, cross-band covariance, variance versus integration time, and ratio distributions. Require state-resolved emission vectors to be independently measured and nonproportional before treating ratio-dispersion changes as a kinetic prediction; if the vectors are proportional, evaluate covariance and ratio statistics as separate estimands. Report equivalent predictive performance as unresolved mechanism identification.

evolution_hints.local_falsifier: The ratio-dispersion component is locally falsified if independently measured proportional state-emission vectors predict invariant noiseless band ratios while observed dispersion is explained by calibrated noise, fitting error, drift, or other nuisance terms. The broader kinetic model is locally falsified if its independently parameterized held-out covariance and window-dependence predictions fail against a preregistered alternative. A residual covariance effect without nonproportional state spectra does not establish a ratio interaction.
evolution_hints.possible_mechanism: A molecule's observed SERS band vector may be a time-weighted result of visits to adsorption environments with different orientations, emission responses, and electromagnetic enhancement. When exchange or residence times are comparable to the acquisition window or molecular reorientation time, this can produce rate-dependent autocovariance, cross-band covariance, and finite-window ratio distributions even when stationary occupancy and mean orientation are matched. The effect is expected to depend on field heterogeneity only through the specified observation model and must be distinguished from established dynamic adsorption, blinking, chemical-enhancement, photochemical, thermal, and instrumental processes.
evolution_hints.research_question: Can independently measured residence and exchange kinetics improve held-out prediction of time-resolved SERS band-vector statistics beyond a broad known-physics model containing static orientation/access, adsorption dynamics, photophysics, chemical enhancement, and instrumental effects, and is any improvement conditional on independently calibrated local-field heterogeneity?

unresolved_attacks.countermodel: Two adsorption states have band vectors (10,5) and (20,10). Both are proportional, so any nonnegative time-weighted mixture has ratio 2.
unresolved_attacks.independent_discriminator: Independent state-specific emission ratio and band-resolved covariance, plus held-out integration-window statistics.

unresolved_attacks.countermodel: Let the two stationary states have band-emission vectors e1=(10,5) and e2=(20,10), with arbitrary common-rate-scaled transition kinetics and any stationary occupancy. Every state vector is proportional to (2,1), so the integrated signal from any trajectory is also proportional to (2,1), apart from additive measurement noise. Kinetic acceleration can therefore change total-intensity covariance and variance while producing no intrinsic finite-window ratio dispersion or high-versus-low-field interaction in the noiseless band ratio.
unresolved_attacks.independent_discriminator: Measure state-specific band vectors and polarization responses independently of pooled ratios, then test whether their vectors are nonproportional across field-heterogeneity strata. Separately compare rate effects on total-intensity covariance with rate effects on ratio dispersion using noise-calibrated data.

evolution_hints.conditional_prediction: In a stationary two-state component, multiplying alpha and beta by lambda while holding beta/(alpha+beta), state emissions, and field statistics fixed predicts tau_corr(lambda)=1/[lambda(alpha+beta)]. The variance of a time-averaged band vector should decrease with T/tau_corr according to the integrated-exponential covariance formula, and finite-window ratio dispersion should generally depend on T/tau_corr because ratios are nonlinear. Under the specified heterogeneous-field observation model, the absolute rate-dependent change in covariance or ratio dispersion may exceed that in the low-heterogeneity control; this is an ordinal, model-conditional interaction prediction rather than a universal expectation. The stationary pooled ratio of time-integrated expected intensities should remain approximately invariant under pure common-rate scaling. Any mean-ratio change requires finite-window nonlinear bias, nonstationarity, state-emission changes, photophysics, chemical enhancement, or another modeled confound.
evolution_hints.decisive_holdout: Jointly preregister predictions for SERS band-vector statistics and an independent adsorption/occupancy trajectory, including held-out kinetics, illumination histories, integration windows, and heterogeneity strata. Require the exchange model to predict both channels without refitting and compare against an observationally matched blinking model.

unresolved_attacks.countermodel: A two-state blinking process with the same transition generator and state emission vectors as a two-state exchange process is observationally equivalent for the measured band-vector trajectory.
unresolved_attacks.independent_discriminator: SERS-independent adsorption occupancy/kinetics channel and illumination-dependent blinking control with matched sampling.

unresolved_attacks.countermodel: Construct a two-state photophysical blinking process with the same transition generator and the same band-emission map as the proposed adsorption-exchange process. Let the hidden states represent emissive and dim or spectrally distinct photophysical states rather than adsorption environments. The resulting band-vector trajectory, including all finite-window means, autocovariances, cross-covariances, and ratio distributions under the observation model, is identical to that of the adsorption-exchange model.
unresolved_attacks.independent_discriminator: Combine the SERS trajectory with an independent adsorption or occupancy channel, such as concentration-jump recovery, interferometric adsorption kinetics, fluorescence exchange, or surface-sensitive relaxation, and repeat the perturbation under matched illumination histories and a blinking control.

evolution_hints.conditional_prediction: Semi-Markov or multi-state models may match sampled covariance yet predict different survival tails, higher-order lag dependence, and integration-time scaling. Independent occupancy kinetics should select among these possibilities conditionally, not establish new physics.
evolution_hints.decisive_holdout: Preregister discrimination among exponential two-state, semi-Markov, and multi-state mixture models using held-out long/short windows, dwell-time survival, higher-order lag statistics, and independent occupancy measurements. Compare predictive calibration without refitting.

evolution_hints.local_falsifier: For the prespecified intervention range, if independently measured kinetics, occupancies, orientations, state emissions, field proxies, detector noise, drift, and broad known-physics nuisance terms produce calibrated out-of-sample predictions of the held-out temporal covariance, window dependence, and ratio distributions in both heterogeneous and low-heterogeneity conditions, then the proposed residence-time-weighted sampling model has no demonstrated explanatory value beyond those established models. Conversely, it is locally falsified as a quantitative kinetic model if its independently parameterized predictions fail reproducibly in the held-out data while a preregistered alternative model accounts for the same statistics. A null change in the pooled mean ratio alone is not a falsifier, and a residual rate effect alone is not proof of a distinct mechanism.
evolution_hints.possible_mechanism: The alternative mechanism is non-Markovian temporal memory: broad dwell-time distributions or unresolved state mixtures, rather than residence-weighted exchange alone, generate the observed SERS statistics. This mechanism predicts history-dependent fluctuations despite matched second-order covariance.
evolution_hints.research_question: Do non-exponential dwell times or unresolved state mixtures improve held-out prediction of time-resolved SERS statistics beyond the original exchange and broad known-physics models?

unresolved_attacks.countermodel: Semi-Markov state dwell distributions and multi-state mixtures may agree on limited second-order statistics while differing in higher-order lag dependence.
unresolved_attacks.independent_discriminator: Held-out long/short integration windows, dwell-time survival curve, multi-lag cross-band temporal tests.

unresolved_attacks.countermodel: Use a semi-Markov two-state process with non-exponential dwell-time distributions and choose its dwell-time survival function, emission amplitudes, and observation noise so that its covariance and cross-covariance at the sampled lags match those of a fitted continuous-time Markov model. Alternatively, use a multi-state Markov mixture whose aggregated second-order statistics match the two-state model while differing in higher-order temporal structure and microscopic residence distributions.
unresolved_attacks.independent_discriminator: Acquire substantially finer and longer trajectories, test the dwell-time survival curve and higher-order lag statistics on held-out data, and compare them with an independent residence or occupancy measurement rather than relying solely on SERS covariance and ratio distributions.
